Abstract

Example Content Guidelines 9.1 is a synthetic recommendation that exists to test how a reader keeps a specification's header, status and dates.

Status of This Document

This section describes the status of this document at the time of its publication. This document was published by the Example Working Group as a Recommendation.

Table of Contents

  1. 1. Perceivable

Introduction

This section is non-normative.

These guidelines explain how content keeps a measured value readable.

1. Perceivable

Content must meet the perceivable principle for every user.

Guideline 1.1 Perceivable guideline

Guideline 1.1 requirement 1: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

Guideline 1.1 requirement 2: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

Guideline 1.1 requirement 3: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

2. Operable

Content must meet the operable principle for every user.

Guideline 2.1 Operable guideline

Guideline 2.1 requirement 1: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

Guideline 2.1 requirement 2: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

Guideline 2.1 requirement 3: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

3. Understandable

Content must meet the understandable principle for every user.

Guideline 3.1 Understandable guideline

Guideline 3.1 requirement 1: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

Guideline 3.1 requirement 2: content that conveys a measured value states its unit and its date in text, so that every reader can perceive both without relying on colour or position.

4. Conformance

This section lists requirements for conformance to these guidelines.

4.1 Conformance requirements

4.1.1 Conformance Level

One of the following levels of conformance is met in full.

  • Level A: For Level A conformance (the minimum level of conformance), the content satisfies all the Level A criteria.

  • Level AA: For Level AA conformance, the content satisfies all the Level A and Level AA criteria.

  • Level AAA: For Level AAA conformance, the content satisfies all the Level A, Level AA and Level AAA criteria.

Criteria per level
LevelCriteria
A12
AA9
AAA7
